title: From Summit to Success: Entrepreneur's Billion-Dollar Lesson from 'Into Thin Air

transcript_chunks.text: I had a high-tech super successful company very young what are the three books that you'd recommend that any entrepreneur should read my favorite that changed my it probably saved my business or helped me understand my business more than anything else at the

time my business was growing so fast but I couldn't quite put my finger on what the problems were I would come home because I'd have these hellaciously stressful days and I would try to read some just so I could sleep and I started

reading Into Thin Air and then it clicked for me what the problem was with my company in the book he talks about everybody has a level where they run out of oxygen when they go up in altitude and even the simplest task when you get

up to a certain level like tying your shoes becomes very very difficult and everybody's built differently and unless you have supplemental oxygen some people will tap out and it becomes deadly and they the only solution is to go down the

mountain but what I was Finding is because my company was growing so fast somebody that was an employee six months ago or a year ago who I hired and was just an amazing employee was failing and it dawned on me what they were really

doing is they were out of oxygen because they had started out and they were working maybe managing four people or six people or ten people and then a year later or six months later they're managing 20 people or 30 people and it's

the same analogy as if you're good at juggling and you can juggle three balls and I hand you a fourth and you're good at that you hand you a fifth a six eventually you're going to reach the level you're going to drop all the balls
and what I realized is it was my responsibility to stop handing them balls and also in some cases take them down the mountain so that book to me saved my company
